preconditions.description: The number of test cases q is an integer between 1 and 10000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(n, int) and isinstance(k, int) and 1 <= k <= n <= 10**6 for n, k in test_cases)
preconditions.description: For each test case, n and k are integers satisfying 1 <= k <= n <= 10^6.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(s, str) and len(s) == n and all(c in '01' for c in s) for (_, _, s) in test_cases)
preconditions.description: For each test case, s is a binary string of length n containing only '0' and '1'.
The sum of n over all test cases does not exceed 10^6.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly 2 lines per test case.

postconditions.expression: all((stdout_lines[2*i] == 'NO' and stdout_lines[2*i+1] == '') or (stdout_lines[2*i] == 'YES' and len(stdout_lines[2*i+1]) == k) for i, (_, k, _) in enumerate(test_cases))
postconditions.description: For each test case, if the answer is NO, the second line is empty; if YES, the second line is a string of length k.

postconditions.expression: all((stdout_lines[2*i] == 'NO' and not any_bit_similar(s, k)) or (stdout_lines[2*i] == 'YES' and is_beautiful(stdout_lines[2*i+1], s, k)) for i, (_, k, s) in enumerate(test_cases))
postconditions.description: For each test case, if NO is printed, no beautiful string exists; if YES is printed, the provided string is beautiful (bit similar to all substrings of length k).

postconditions.expression: all((stdout_lines[2*i] == 'NO') or (stdout_lines[2*i+1] == min_beautiful(s, k)) for i, (_, k, s) in enumerate(test_cases))
postconditions.description: For each test case where a solution exists, the printed string is the lexicographically smallest beautiful string.
